thread:
support-alex: FYI ACME (acct: acme-inc) opened an escalation — sudden p99 jump starting ~2026-03-10T14:05Z. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~400ms, p99 ~5-7s. Some 504s reported. Sample request ids: rq_abc123, rq_def456. Repro curl below.

support-alex: ```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Acct: acme-inc' \
  -d '{"input":"summarize...","model":"gpt-small"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
```

eng-maria: Thanks — can you paste the small log snippet + which models/routes affected? Any recent deploys to serving-runtime around 14:00? :mag:

support-alex: Logs attached (trimmed):

support-alex: ```
[14:05:12] rq=rq_abc123 route=/v1/generate status=200 latency=5200ms worker=wm-12 queued=18
[14:05:15] rq=rq_def456 route=/v1/embeddings status=504 worker=wm-09 queued=22 admit=throttled
[14:06:02] rq=rq_xyz789 route=/v1/generate status=200 latency=6100ms worker=wm-14 queued=21
```

oncall-jordan: Seeing same in metrics — admission_queue_length spiked from <5 to ~20 at ~14:03 UTC, worker_utilization at 92% on the serving pool. Also a small roll at 13:58 but nothing major in image. My hunch: pile-up on long-running streaming/generation requests causing head-of-line queueing.

sre-ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0453; alert: emit_admit_queue>15 for pool=prod-serving.

platform-lee: Quick check: top tenant by QPS in that window is acme-inc (bursting). I also see a handful of streaming sessions that held workers for >4s each. Fairness settings currently allow 100 concurrent per-tenant but global concurrency limit is tight.

eng-maria: If it's tenant burst + long tails, admission controller might be letting small/short requests starve. Two quick mitigations we can try:
1) Temporarily reduce per-stream concurrency for acme-inc OR set them to lower streaming weight.
2) Increase tenant reserved concurrency for acme-inc for short requests or route them to dedicated pool (if on Dedicated plan).

oncall-jordan: Can we do a 10m hotfix first: bump acme-inc soft concurrency from 100 -> 140 and enable short-request prioritization? Admin API below.

platform-lee: Also add an immediate admission-controller rule to deprioritize streaming sessions by using expected_job_duration heuristic.

eng-maria: Admin API to bump reservation (run with ops key):

eng-maria: ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://internal-admin.redwood/v1/tenants/acme-inc/reservations \
  -d '{"soft_concurrency":140, "priority_profile":"short-first"}'
```

oncall-jordan: Applied soft_concurrency=140 at 14:12:07 UTC. Also pushed a temporary admission rule (deprioritize stream:true for 30m) at 14:13:10 UTC. Will watch p99.

platform-lee: Small caveat — bumping soft_concurrency may increase cost; customer on support call ok with temporary uplift.

support-alex: ACME confirmed they saw immediate improvement on their side; p99 reported down to ~900ms at 14:20. They asked for a short RCA and next steps.

eng-maria: Good — collect metrics for 30m window. Root cause hypothesis: tenant burst of long-running streaming/generate requests combined with fairness policy that didn't separate streaming vs short requests. Action items:
- short (0-1s expected) prioritization flag in admission controller (P0 for next week).
- telemetry: add per-tenant streaming_ratio metric to alert if >0.5 for 5m.
- ops runbook: temporary soft_concurrency bump + enable short-first policy.

sre-ops-bot: Action logged: ACME mitigation applied, monitor window started (14:13 UTC). Ticket updated.

oncall-jordan: Will keep this thread open for final RCA. If p99 holds under 1s for 30m, we'll close with postmortem steps.

support-alex: Customer call scheduled 14:45 UTC; I'll share interim notes. :white_check_mark:

platform-lee: For follow-up — schedule a small rollback test on staging of the admission heuristic change, and draft the admission-controller config patch (PR ready: branch/adm-prioritize-short). I can cut the PR after triage.

eng-maria: Noted. Thanks everyone, good coordination. Closing loop after 14:45 check-in.

customer-acme: Thanks for the quick response team — saw much better perf after the change. Appreciate the fast fix.
